text:
sam-cs: Hey team, customer on private VPC reported invoice much higher than dashboard for Feb 27-28. They say dashboard shows ~1.2M tokens but invoice shows ~1.9M. Agent is the on-prem meter in their VPC (agent v1.12.3). Can we look?

elaine-ops: Thanks Sam. Any quick diffs in agent logs or upload history? Customer says they had a network outage ~2026-02-28T03:10Z for ~7m.

sam-cs: They attached a small log snippet and ledger export. It looks like there were a couple of flushes where the agent retried and the same batch landed twice in the collector. Also they reported host time was manually adjusted during the outage.

tom-eng: Ok initial theory: local monotonic counter/seq got reset or timestamp jumps caused collector to accept duplicates when replay window overlapped. Need a minimal repro and a quick script to check ledger events for duplicates by event_id and seq.

ryan-infra: Can you grab these from the agent node: `/var/lib/redwood/meter/ledger.json` and the upload history at `/var/log/redwood/meter/uploader.log`? Look for repeated `flush_id` and identical token counts. Also check `dmesg` / `syslog` for clock changes (NTP step).

sam-cs: Pasted the output they provided:
```
# ledger.json events (excerpt)
{"seq": 124130, "flush_id": "f-20260228-0310-1", "tokens": 41234, "event_id": "ev-81c6"}
{"seq": 124131, "flush_id": "f-20260228-0310-1", "tokens": 41234, "event_id": "ev-81c6"}
{"seq": 124132, "flush_id": "f-20260228-0310-2", "tokens": 98312, "event_id": "ev-81c7"}
```
uploader.log shows a successful POST for `f-20260228-0310-1` at 03:11:05 then another POST at 03:12:02 with identical body (server accepted both, returned 200). Syslog has: `Mar 28 03:10:55 host ntpd[123]: step time server 192.0.2.1 magnitude 320s`

elaine-ops: That lines up. If the host time was stepped forward, some local monotonic sequencing logic in the agent might have ended up writing the same event twice during buffered retries, and collector accepted because it keyed on timestamp+flush_id (not strictly dedupe-safe).

tom-eng: Quick checks I want from the customer: (1) full ledger.json between seq 124120-124140, (2) uploader.log between 03:08-03:15Z, (3) the raw POST bodies we received at the collector (if available) or server-side ingestion logs. For us: grep collector logs for `event_id ev-81c6` and `flush_id f-20260228-0310-1`.

sam-cs: Customer uploaded ledger slice and uploader.log to support bucket; shared link: https://internal-s3.example/redwood/support/priv-1234/ledgers/2026-02-28.zip

ryan-infra: I pulled collector logs. There are two ingestion lines: `ingest: accepted batch flush f-20260228-0310-1 size=41k batch_id=b-9901` at 03:11:06 and `ingest: accepted batch flush f-20260228-0310-1 size=41k batch_id=b-9902` at 03:12:03. No dedupe detected. Payload bodies are identical except `client_sent_at` header differs by 57s.

tom-eng: Two things to fix short term: (A) issue credits for duplicated tokens while we investigate and (B) implement a server-side dedupe filter by `event_id` (idempotency) for the ingestion pipeline. For the customer: ask them to avoid time adjustments on agent hosts while agent is active; enforce NTP step restrictions.

elaine-ops: Sam — go ahead and offer a pro-rated credit for the ~700k extra tokens and mention we're investigating. I can draft the wording.

sam-cs: Will do. Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate we fixed it. Any safe repro?

tom-eng: Repro suggestion (non-destructive): On a test node run the meter agent, simulate a network partition and a clock jump forward ~60s, then resume network so uploader retries and agent re-flushes same batch. Script (for test cluster only):
```bash
# step 1: run agent capture for ~10s
sudo systemctl stop ntp || true
python3 -m redwood_meter_agent --capture --output /tmp/ledger.json &
AGENT_PID=$!
# step 2: simulate network block
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP
sleep 5
# step 3: step clock forward (test node only)
sudo date -s "+65 seconds"
# step 4: unblock network so agent retries
sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP
sleep 10
# check ledger and uploader.log for duplicate flushes
kill $AGENT_PID
```
Note: only run in isolated test env. We can't recommend customers change system time in prod.

ryan-infra: Long-term fixes: (1) agent should use monotonic counters separate from wall clock for sequencing, (2) uploader should include an idempotency-key (event_id) and collector should dedupe on that, (3) add a post-flush checksum verification and reject exact-duplicate bodies if recognized within replay window.

tom-eng: I'll open a GH issue and a quick-hotfix PR to add server-side dedupe by `event_id` for ingestion (config flaggable so we can roll it). Also add a metric on duplicate ingestion attempts.

elaine-ops: I filed the customer credit and sent an apology note. Sam — copy of notes to customer: we recommend pinning NTP configs and applying the agent update that enforces monotonic seqs when we release it (ETA 2 weeks).

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1547 (private-meter-duplicate-ingest). Assigned: tom-eng. Priority: P2.

sam-cs: Thanks all — I'll confirm the credit and share the repro with the customer. Follow-ups: Tom, please paste the PR link when available and Ryan, can you add the duplicate metric to the console so we can alert if this spikes?

tom-eng: Will do. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/r/infra/ingest/pulls/412 (draft).

ryan-infra: Adding duplicate_ingest.count metric to the console dashboard now. ETA 3 days.

sam-cs: Closing loop with customer now, leaving thread open for PR/metric updates. Thanks.
